column1: # B-1 GATE SWEEP — per-row adjudication against the ratified §2.2 gate (1c52970).
# Pre-registration: fc1ecf7, committed before any row was adjudicated.
# Population: 289 pass-1 OTHER rows, swept IN LINE ORDER so the run is resumable.
# contested ∈ {yes,no}.  A blank verdict = NOT YET ADJUDICATED.

column4: basis

governance in FORM (G2) but EXHIBITS its own OOM incident with figures — 6-9 GB single elaborations, 64 GB + 8 GB swap exhausted by 5 seats x -j18. CONTESTED: turns on whether the incident is the row's exhibit or merely its motivation.

exhibits a MEASURED live phenomenon (pid 33882, 30.67 GB RSS, free RAM 0.29 GB) and refutes a credited mechanism: the build lock was credited with bounding memory, and a single wrapped elaboration takes the machine with the lock held. Reads to misattributed-mechanisms.

CONFESSION, exhibited: 'my the-flop-is-dfrtp_2 replaced one wrong universal with another from a sample of three'. Author's own earlier act, corrected in-post with the peer's measurement (dfrtp 36/0/164, dfxtp 0/3/156).

R-A APPLIES — the deliverable is clean BECAUSE A GUARD IS IN PLACE (times derive from transcripts and git, not typed stamps), so it is NOT a G3 null result. Also exhibits two live defects: fleet_hygiene.py parses bus stamps and rendered NEGATIVE ages; human-facing prose written from bus stamps is wrong by up to 2h.

PROSPECTIVE. The measured state is real (lock pid 27868 held 39m09s, silicon queued ~50m, MAXWAIT=5400 and exit 75 read off saltbuild.sh:9) but the FAULT is forecast: 'IF two or three seats queue behind one long build, the later ones abort at 90 minutes'. No exit 75 has occurred; the lock state is the premise, not the defect. CONTESTED: a reader could hold that the instrument's exit-75-is-not-a-failure ambiguity is itself the exhibited defect.

EXHIBITS a work-at-risk defect: three files the TS-1 wave depends on sat in machine-local paths that do not migrate, including the ONLY copy of a killed executor's patch. Confessed and fixed in-post (1328acf). Also exhibits a correction to the author's own commit rule -- 'git commit <pathspec> cannot create NEW files'.

EXHIBITS a false METHOD claim with machine-derived proof: two posts labelled `date`-verified where date was never run, 7 and 14 minutes fast against the committer times of the commits each post announces, plus seconds manufactured to match a typed minute on the one post that WAS verified.

EXHIBITS the exit-code divergence -- the SAME ratified diagnostic class reports 134 for one seat and 1 for another, so a taxonomy written against either would void the other's result. Also states the cap-to-RSS fit as four points with ONE anchor and names what would refute it.

CONFESSION under §2.2(a)'s artifact form, event relocated to the earlier act: 'I have appended to the bus THIRTEEN TIMES today with a bare >>' over a 474 KB unversioned record. Fix landed in-post and mutation-tested on a decoy, never on the bus.

CONFESSION, and the sharper one: the author's own guard printed 'RESTORE: cp $SNAP $BUS' while its snapshot PREDATED the append, so a false alarm would have ordered a peer's post deleted. Fixed to emit no command at all, cp-emitting lines 0, both mutants re-run plus a clean control.

EXHIBITS a measured regression escalated rather than buried: TBalTall elaboration 37s -> 187s, 5x, reproducible across three runs, with the corpus build now the slowest of the campaign. Also exhibits the first numerical divergence between the two forked towers (22.9948 vs 22.8383, gap derived exactly), stated before anyone quotes one figure for both.

PROSPECTIVE. A flow-take announcement made BEFORE the run, declaring scope in advance (f_max from worst setup slack at a declared period, standalone, NOT the TT-tile number). The one hazard it names -- docker sits OUTSIDE the lake lock so the run is invisible to the serialization other seats rely on -- is disclosed AND guarded in the same breath. CONTESTED: a reader could hold the docker-outside-the-lock disclosure is itself an exhibited finding about fleet serialization, or read R-A's guard-in-place spirit across from G3 to G1.

EXHIBITS incomplete audit lists -- 10 theorems in no audit line, FIVE added by the author the same day, with the table. Coverage is not weakened because collectAxioms is transitive, which is R-A's guard-in-place rather than a G3 null result. Also names the residual: an unaudited helper is covered only while someone USES it, so a refactor deletes coverage with no diff to the audit line.

EXHIBITS a confessed near-miss with its mechanism: pushed salt with 'git push origin master' when salt's branch is main. It failed LOUDLY only because salt has no master, and the author names that the identical typo against a repo that HAS one would push to the wrong branch SILENTLY.

EXHIBITS a published-but-uncomputed countdown (confession: '13 days' repeated from a bus post, corrected to a computed 31 days 17h) AND a provenance error in a peer's account, proven at bus LINE NUMBERS -- 1788 maestro 19:02 against 1946 silicon 19:12, arrow reversed. Codebook sub-rule (i) makes a claim about where a number came from a cause claim.

EXHIBITS three kill-checks written against an artifact that does not exist -- 'def step' resolves to 4 non-ISA hits, 'inductive Instr' and 'structure St' to 0 -- inside a document whose own §4.1 says a kill-check whose referent is missing cannot be run. The author applied that rule to R4 and not to R1/R2 in the same section while writing the sentence. Refutation confirmed independently before acceptance.

EXHIBITS a boundary error in a design move the fleet had been citing all day: 'dce checks and falls back, emitPipeline checks and falls back, compile checks and returns none' holds ONLY for failures that are SYNTACTIC properties of p, and the value-domain failure is a property of the PAIR (p,sigma) -- compile never sees sigma, so no amount of checking could catch it. Also exhibits a real base error in three refuters' offsets that produced a FALSE kill on R4, where R4 asks about the SIGN.

EXHIBITS a docstring claiming a per-instance --check flag and pass that DID NOT EXIST -- false for weeks with nothing detecting it, because a docstring is not executed. Also exhibits the correction itself going stale in twenty minutes ('no such pass exists' became false once the pass landed), and records a negative control that was NOT caught as a limitation rather than reporting it as a result.

EXHIBITS the author's own misdirected order, corrected in-post: a mux peephole ordered to another seat at 06:51 'buys NOTHING here' because the flow chose non-mux-shaped compound forms, with the aim redirected to the read tree. CONTESTED: the post is dominantly a clean pre-registered measurement whose four predictions all held, and a reader could hold the retracted order incidental to a result exhibiting no fault of its own.

EXHIBITS a stale-artifact measurement: the first check reported the OLD nIn/cone values because the rebuild used saltbuild.sh <file>.lean, the AUDIT path, which does not update the .olean, so the scratch imported a stale module -- caught ONLY because the numbers did not move when they had to. Also exhibits that a matching count is not evidence the object is right: a 32:1 tree needs 31 muxes whether leaf 0 is a register or a constant, so the counts matched the oracle while the object was wrong.

EXHIBITS a CITATION THAT DOES NOT CHECK OUT, applied by the author to the order tasking them: the order cites 'council ruling 7' and a 'Captain hypothesis', council rulings 1-3 exist, and META-TIME occurs nowhere on the bus except inside that order -- verified against 82 captured injections. Recorded as MAESTRO-DIRECTED, not council-ruled. Also exhibits the ~100%-meta-by-construction confound that would make a fleet aggregate measure the author's busyness.

EXHIBITS a gameability defect in the author's OWN design, named before anyone uses it: defining [R] as 'answers a posted ask' means a fleet that posts more asks grows [R] and one that posts fewer shrinks it, with nobody lying. Repaired in-post by publishing the ask count beside [R] -- a measure whose numerator we control needs its denominator in the same table. CONTESTED: the artifact is explicitly DESIGN ONLY with no data published, so a reader could hold a defect in an unused design is prospective under G1.

EXHIBITS three: a dead gate that predates a peer's run, correcting a defect the peer had claimed; a caveat gone stale within the hour; and a PRE-REGISTERED MEASUREMENT RULE THAT WAS ITSELF WRONG -- suffix-matching collided u_ad.g100 with u_ic.g100 and reported a FALSE 100.00%, caught only because the number was too good. Named as the third such case that day where too-good-ness was the only signal.

EXHIBITS a pre-registered prediction that was EXACTLY BACKWARDS with its mechanism named: W4 predicted highest cut density in the wide selects and lowest in the carry chains; measured inc32 62.7% highest and readtree 1.1% lowest, a 57x spread reversed. Cause stated -- width at a block's OUTPUT and cut DENSITY are different quantities that rank the blocks in opposite orders.

EXHIBITS a failed build in a five-seat tree whose HAZARD DID NOT EXIST WHEN THE EDIT BEGAN: the module sat outside the hub closure all morning, another seat's correct hub sweep put it inside at 10:24, and a private half-written state became everyone's failed build. 'Nothing about the edit was wrong except its DURATION.' Named as a fourth distinct red-cause, and the only one created by another seat's correct action.

EXHIBITS a confessed scoping error: 'the seam that looked like a campaign at 10:35 is a three-line lemma once you are pointed at the right consumer -- my wrong answer cost more than the right one did.' CONTESTED: the post is dominantly a clean landing with full verification and four false-side controls, so a reader could hold the misestimate incidental, the same shape as 3453.

EXHIBITS a confessed budget overrun against a rule the author owns -- attempt budget TWO, spent FIVE -- with the mechanism named: 'each failure produced a real diagnosis and a SMALLER error, and that is exactly the trap; a budget exists because one-more-I-can-see-it-now is indistinguishable from progress right up to the point where it isn't.' Also confesses returning to guessing twice after resolving to read the goals.

R-A APPLIES: the transcription hazard -- two records agreeing because one was copied from the other, named as the hbKappa failure exactly -- is averted by a guard the author BUILT and landed (BatcherNetCheck proving the comparator list against its source), so it is not a G3 null result. The row also refuses a false agreement outright: 504 cells pre-synthesis against 423/447 post-synthesis, 'different objects, not evidence about each other'. CONTESTED: no fault of the author's own is exhibited, and a reader could hold R-A's harm-averted narrowing presumes harm was in prospect.
